notes.claim: UK domestic supply is nominally 230 V, 50 Hz, kept within 216 V to 253 V by the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations.
Ships mostly run 60 Hz, because higher frequency lets motors and generators run faster and so be smaller for a given power.

sources.title: Statutory Voltage Limits – Energy Networks Association (ENA)
sources.quote: UK mains electricity operates at a nominal voltage of 230V, and can operate within limits of 253V and 216V set by the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations (ESQCR)

sources.title: maritime electrical installations - notes on design ...
sources.quote: 60 Hz is the most common frequency adopted for use on board ship; the higher frequency enabling motors and generators to run at higher speeds with a consequent reduction in size for a given power rating.
